title: Chicken Schnitzel
subtitle: Pan-fried breaded chicken breast
excerpt: Chicken schnitzel is a weeknight favourite: thin, crisp-breaded chicken cooked quickly in a hot pan. Butterflying and bashing the breast thin is the key step that ensures even cooking and a shatteringly light crust.
sourceNotes: Schnitzel is a staple of German and Austrian cooking, traditionally made with veal. Chicken schnitzel follows the same breading and frying technique and is a popular everyday version.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze breaded uncooked schnitzels on a lined tray, then transfer to bags. Cook from frozen, adding 5 minutes to the cooking time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bread the chicken up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerate uncovered. Cook just before serving.

content.text: Chicken schnitzel relies on one essential step: getting the breast thin and even before it touches the breadcrumbs. Butterfly each breast by slicing it horizontally almost in two, then open it out and bash it with a rolling pin until it is about 5mm thick. This gives you a large, flat piece that fries in minutes and stays juicy inside while the coating turns golden and crisp.

Panko breadcrumbs give a lighter, crunchier finish than standard breadcrumbs. Fry in batches so the pan stays hot; crowding the pan drops the temperature and the coating steams rather than crisps. Serve with lemon wedges and a simple green salad or potato salad.

Butterfly each chicken breast: place it flat on a board and slice horizontally almost all the way through, then open it out like a book. Cover with cling film and bash firmly with a rolling pin until the meat is about 5mm thick throughout. Season both sides with salt and black pepper.

Set up three shallow bowls: one with the flour, one with the beaten eggs, and one with the panko breadcrumbs. Working one piece at a time, coat the chicken in flour and shake off any excess, dip into the egg letting the surplus drip off, then press into the breadcrumbs so both sides are evenly covered.

Pour half the oil into the frying pan and set it over a medium-high heat. When the oil is hot and shimmering, add two schnitzels. Fry for 3 to 4 minutes on the first side without moving them, until the underside is deep golden. Flip and cook for a further 2 to 3 minutes until cooked through.
Transfer the cooked schnitzels to a plate lined with kitchen paper and keep warm in a low oven. Add the remaining oil to the pan and cook the second batch in the same way.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges for squeezing over.

items.symptom: The coating falls off during frying
items.cause: The flour layer was too thick or the egg did not adhere properly.
items.fix: Shake off excess flour firmly before the egg dip. Press the breadcrumbs on with your hands and allow the breaded schnitzel to rest for 5 minutes before frying so the coating firms up.

items.symptom: The coating is pale and greasy
items.cause: The oil was not hot enough when the chicken went in.
items.fix: Wait until the oil shimmers and a breadcrumb dropped in sizzles immediately. Keep the heat at medium-high throughout.

items.symptom: The chicken is overcooked and dry inside
items.cause: The breast was not bashed thin enough, so the outside overcooked before the centre was done.
items.fix: Aim for a consistent 5mm thickness. At that thickness, 3 to 4 minutes per side over medium-high heat is enough.

items.symptom: The coating burns before the chicken is cooked through
items.cause: The breast is too thick in places or the heat is too high.
items.fix: Bash more evenly next time. If the coating is browning too fast, lower the heat slightly and cover the pan loosely for the last minute.
